text.p: The following are some leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
Communist-led union group CGTP says rejects 2.6 per cent as a starting point for the 1998 public employee wage negotiations.
Opposition Social Democrats demand special parliamentary session to debate expulsion of Portuguese ambassador from South Africa.
UGT and CGTP union groupings unanimous in rejecting 2.6 percent. Government was reporting to be considering offering between 2.6 and 2.9 percent for 1998.
Lisbon will have six more hotels by the opening of Expo '98 next May. By the end of the century, the number of rooms in the city will have risen 20 percent.
State-controlled energy company Petrogal has had negotiations on taking a stake of up to 50 percent in Moroccan company Somepi, the paper quotes Moroccan sources as saying.
